Well-motivated problem formulation (multicollinearity in representation-based CL) with clear visualization of progressive decorrelation across pipeline stages (Figure 3)

Well-documented implementation with clear hyperparameters, experimental setup, and reproducibility considerations

Practical value for edge deployment avoiding model storage overhead compared to mixture-based approaches

Significant practical efficiency gains: 67-91% reduction in post-extraction training time while maintaining or improving accuracy across datasets
Solid theoretical analysis with rigorous complexity bounds (Theorems 4.1-4.2) and elegant connection between Hebbian learning and ridge classification (Section 6)

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: sparse random projection, top-k sparsification, and ridge regression are all standard techniques; primary contribution is their combination, which is incremental for a top-tier venue

Missing statistical rigor: results include ±std but no significance tests; some improvements marginal (0.32% on CIFAR-100); unclear if differences are statistically significant
Limited ablation scope: no empirical comparison of dense vs. sparse projection; alternative k-selection strategies unexplored; different correlation measures for multicollinearity not investigated

Well-organized presentation with effective visualizations and extensive reproducibility details in appendices
